stdout: Format Vue, JSX, and TSX files Usage: vize fmt [OPTIONS] [PATTERNS]... Arguments: [PATTERNS]... Vue/JS/TS/JSON/JSONC globs; YAML/Markdown formatting is not implemented [default: ./**/*.vue ./**/*.js ./**/*.mjs ./**/*.cjs ./**/*.ts ./**/*.mts ./**/*.cts ./**/*.jsx ./**/*.tsx ./**/*.json ./**/*.jsonc] Options: --check Check formatting without writing (exit with error if files need formatting) -w, --write Write formatted output to files -c, --config Config file path --no-config Do not load a config file --single-quote[=] Use single quotes instead of double quotes [possible values: true, false] --jsx-single-quote[=] Use single quotes in JSX attributes [possible values: true, false] --quote-props Change when object properties are quoted Possible values: - as-needed: Quote only properties that require quotes - consistent: Quote every property when one property requires quotes - preserve: Preserve whether each property was authored with quotes --trailing-comma Change where trailing commas are printed Possible values: - all: Print trailing commas wherever possible - es5: Print trailing commas where valid in ES5 - none: Do not print trailing commas --arrow-parens Change parentheses around a sole arrow function parameter Possible values: - always: Always include parentheses around a sole parameter - avoid: Omit parentheses when a sole parameter permits it --bracket-spacing[=] Print spaces inside object literal braces [possible values: true, false] --bracket-same-line[=] Put the closing bracket of a multi-line tag on its last attribute line [possible values: true, false] --end-of-line Choose the line ending written by the formatter Possible values: - lf: Line feed - crlf: Carriage return followed by line feed - cr: Carriage return - auto: Preserve the first line ending found in the source --print-width Print width (line length) for formatting --tab-width Number of spaces per indentation level --use-tabs[=] Use tabs instead of spaces for indentation [possible values: true, false] --semi[=] Print semicolons at the ends of statements [possible values: true, false] --no-semi Do not print semicolons at the ends of statements --sort-attributes[=] Sort HTML attributes in template [possible values: true, false] --attribute-sort-order Choose the order of attributes within each Vue priority group Possible values: - alphabetical: Sort alphabetically within each priority group - as-written: Preserve the authored order within each priority group --single-attribute-per-line[=] Put each HTML attribute on its own line [possible values: true, false] --vue-indent-script-and-style[=] Indent script and style block contents [possible values: true, false] --max-attributes-per-line Maximum number of attributes per line before wrapping --normalize-directive-shorthands[=] Normalize directive shorthands (v-bind: → :, v-on: → @, v-slot: → #) [possible values: true, false] --sort-blocks[=] Order SFC blocks canonically instead of preserving their authored order [possible values: true, false] --self-close-void-elements[=] Close HTML void elements such as `` with `/>` [possible values: true, false] --normalize-css-quotes[=] Normalize CSS, SCSS and Less string quotes using the string quote preference [possible values: true, false] --normalize-inline-styles[=] Normalize plain static style attributes as one-line CSS declarations [possible values: true, false] --normalize-v-for-parens[=] Parenthesize multiple v-for aliases [possible values: true, false] --reindent-preprocessor-styles[=] Re-indent SCSS and Less block contents by nesting depth [possible values: true, false] --preset Apply a named set of defaults before the flags above Possible values: - vize: The Vize defaults - prettier: Prettier's Vue layout, as listed in the formatter guide - compact: Dense application layout that preserves authored order - documentation: Readable documentation examples with one attribute per line --profile Show detailed timing profile --slow-threshold Slow file threshold in milliseconds for profile output [default: 100] -h, --help Print help (see a summary with '-h')
